findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: OpenCode 2's serve may already bind loopback by default and refuse a non-loopback bind without an explicit flag, making the omitted flag redundant; the repository cannot confirm this and runner network isolation would mask it in CI.
findingDetails.claim: The battery's private server bind address is left to OpenCode 2's default, so the loopback posture its client and port probe assume is unverified.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the file for host pinning: only findFreePort (probe.listen(0,'127.0.0.1')) and the client serverUrl name loopback; the spawn carries no host flag. Diff check shows the spawn is unchanged by the merge. waitForBanner requires a listening line and a password before any request, so pre-auth exposure is limited.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to a note once serve is shown to default to loopback; escalate to P1 if the default binds every interface, since the child then serves the caller's credentials beyond the host boundary.
findingDetails.scopeProof: File is inside the declared review scope; the serve spawn is a context line in git diff 06d02096e90^1 06d02096e90, so the posture is inherited in a reviewed file rather than introduced by the merge.
findingDetails.title: The doctor battery starts its private OpenCode 2 server without pinning the bind address, while handing it the whole parent environment

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Ignoring an unsupported key may equal the host ignoring it, and warning on every unmapped key would be noise while the set is small and stable; the counter is that a hard guard degrading to a no-op should fail loudly rather than fail open.
findingDetails.claim: dualPlugin silently ignores hook keys outside MAPPED_HOOKS, so a guard that registers an unmapped key loads without effect and without any failing signal.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the whole setup path for a warn or throw on skippedKeys: none. Both shipped guard plugins use tool.execute.before, which is mapped, so the drop is latent. The six-entry set is the bridge's own translation table, so the drop is the bridge's decision.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to a note if the registration test family asserts each guard plugin's hook keys are all in MAPPED_HOOKS, or if the host rejects unknown keys before the bridge sees them. Escalate to P1 if a shipped guard plugin registers a key outside the set.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Bridge and plugins are inside the declared review scope; the claim is limited to the mapping table and the drop path, and the guard plugins were read only to establish that their keys are mapped.
findingDetails.title: An unmapped plugin hook key is dropped with no runtime signal, so a guard plugin's block can silently become a no-op on OpenCode 2

noveltyJustification: Both weighted findings this iteration are new P2s and there were no refinements or re-counted carried-forward findings, so the weighted-new share is 1.0 by composition rather than by discovery density. Most of the iteration re-confirmed clean surfaces: the trust seam's injection resistance, the rewritten remove-v1 mutation surface, the session reader's read-only fixed SQL, and the shell-free fanout spawn.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Security review of merged runtime, CI and plugin code across 22 files with two actionable findings; not a trivial target.

searchLedger.invariant: the probe executes only a file the operator already put in reach, never the command's own spelling
searchLedger.rationale: No path lets a command-supplied string reach spawn as the executed binary, and spawn is shell-free.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: verified by direct read of both resolvers and the spawn helpers

searchActions.result: identity comparison on canonical path, size and mtime; probe runs the trusted path; executableFile rejects a literal non-path before any spawn

searchLedger.hypothesis: a launcher name or path can make the dispatch guard skip rules
searchLedger.rationale: Every branch applies all four appliesToAll rules, so no name or path buys an unchecked dispatch.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: all four shipped rules declare appliesTo [v2] and both filters converge on applying every rule

searchActions.result: undetected dispatches leave filterByVersion false, so the version continue never fires; unresolved families take every rule

searchLedger.invariant: every refusal precedes the first write and only the helper's own launcher is deleted
searchLedger.rationale: Mutations are narrowed relative to the parent and every refusal runs before the first write; the residual check-to-remove window is not a privilege boundary.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: same-authority window, rm on a symlink unlinks only the link

searchActions.result: multi-name mv/rm/ln/chmod loop replaced by one rm -- on the launcher plus a quoted mv -- to a hidden aside path and a constant-operand npm uninstall

searchLedger.hypothesis: the private server's password or inherited environment reaches the uploaded JSON artifact
searchLedger.rationale: The artifact path is clean, but the child inherits the full environment (v2ServerEnv spreading env) while its bind address is left to the package default, which is the residual exposure recorded as DR2-P2-001.

searchActions.result: password captured by waitForBanner and used only to build apiEnv; no result field or log line carries it

searchLedger.hypothesis: a plugin hook the bridge does not map silently stops enforcing
searchLedger.rationale: A guard key outside the mapping table loads without effect and without a failing signal; both shipped guards happen to use a mapped key, so the risk is latent.

searchActions.result: skippedKeys computed against a six-entry set and attached only to the cleanup function; no throw, log or registration assertion

searchLedger.hypothesis: command text, prompt text or a database name is interpolated into SQL or a shell
searchLedger.rationale: No dynamic SQL and no shell interpretation on either path.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: direct read of both producers shows fixed statements and shell-free spawns

searchActions.result: fixed sqlite_master statement on a readOnly connection; spawn without a shell; prompt kept out of the fingerprint behind a digest; rerun commands quoted with a strict allowlist

omittedHighRiskTargets: opencode serve's default bind implementation (lives in the installed package, not this tree)
targetSelection.selectionReason: Producer/consumer pairing from the dispatched focus: each security surface named in the iteration prompt was read at its producing and consuming site.

results.summary: Two documented security claims hold in code: remove-v1's refusals all precede the first write and data files are only listed, and the battery's private-server password reaches only apiEnv, never a result field or log line.

detail: security: 2 new P2, 0 P1, 0 P0. The version trust seam, the rewritten remove-v1 mutation surface, the session reader SQL and the fanout spawn were re-read and found clean; the residual risks are an unverified bind default on a long-lived child holding the caller environment, and a silent hook-mapping drop on the plugin guard path.

summary: remove-v1 refusal order and data-file non-mutation hold in code; the battery password reaches only apiEnv.

direction: A launcher name or path bypasses the dispatch guard
reason: An undetected dispatch leaves filterByVersion false so the version continue never fires, and an unresolved family takes every rule; all four rules declare appliesTo [v2].

direction: OPENCODE_BIN widens the executable trust set to an attacker-named file
reason: fileIdentity returns null for an unreadable path and the probe runs the trusted path, not the command spelling.

direction: The remove-v1 check-to-remove window lets a swap delete a foreign file
reason: rm on a symlink unlinks the link and the swap needs the user own directory write authority.

direction: The session reader builds SQL from command text; fanout builds a shell command
reason: Fixed sqlite_master statement on a readOnly connection; spawn without a shell and prompts kept out of the fingerprint behind a digest.
